units.text: Fog lies on the valley like spilled milk.
Two lanes of trucks idle in a row, exhaust rising straight up in the windless cold.
A loudspeaker coughs somewhere, then gives up.
A faded sign reads: ALL VEHICLES STOP.
Under it, a stray dog sleeps against a concrete barrier, ribs rising and falling.
Eleven years at this crossing, and I can tell you how a man lies by how he holds his steering wheel. Tight means fear. Loose means practice. This one held it like a baby bird.
units.name: NARRATOR

units.text: A grey hatchback rolls to the booth.
Behind the glass, INSPECTOR HALVORSEN, 50s, heavy, unhurried, a thermos steaming beside his keyboard, lifts one finger.
